track: Neural and AI routes to photorealism in 2026: real-time enhancement, neural rendering, world models and AI-assisted assets
summary:
Not on this Mac, and not while the LiDAR stays the source of truth. Neural rendering in 2026 falls into two families.

The first is engine-guided re-rendering: the engine supplies the geometry and a generative model supplies photographic appearance. It is the only family compatible with the fidelity rule, and it now runs in real time, but only on large NVIDIA GPUs:
- DLSS 5: RTX 50 only, on Windows, with a reported 40–60% frame-rate cost;
- REGEN: over 20 fps at 960×544 on an RTX 4090;
- research renderers: about 30 fps on one H100 or H200.

The best measured real-time diffusion on Apple silicon is 22.7 fps at 512×512 on an M3 Ultra. That implies about 2–3 fps on this Air before Godot draws anything. Godot has no neural hooks beyond MetalFX upscaling.

The second family is interactive world models (Genie 3, Odyssey-2, HY-World, Marble, Atlas). They look photographic for 60 seconds to a few minutes, but they invent geometry. DeepMind says Genie 3 cannot reproduce real places accurately. An independent benchmark found that scene memory decays by 37% over 10–60-second walks.

AI asset tools help with rocks, logs and textures but still fail on thin branching structure, so the tree cap stands.

I measured the owner's photos and Godot's renders with the project's lighting tool. Godot's lighting is already inside or at the edge of the photos' range for exposure key, sunflecks, blacks and highlight colour. What is missing is structure and about 3 stops of dynamic range.

A photographic look is reachable in two ways only:
- offline, with depth-conditioned video models on a rented H100 at about $3.25 an hour;
- interactively, with an RTX 50 PC or a paid cloud stream.

findings.claim: The one shipping product that re-renders game frames to read as photographic is NVIDIA DLSS 5 ('3D-guided neural rendering'). It has been live since 3 September 2026 in NBA 2K27. A one-step pixel-space diffusion transformer takes the engine frame plus G-buffers (albedo, normals, depth, motion vectors) and adds photographic lighting and materials, including light passing through foliage. Developers can mask it. Limits: GeForce RTX 50 only (RTX 40 promised 'soon'); integration through Streamline or an Unreal plugin; reported as very heavy (Digital Foundry measured 40–60% frame-rate loss, and early demos used a second RTX 5090). It has no Metal, macOS or Godot path. NVIDIA's own pages were blocked here, so this rests on search snippets.

Research 'photorealism enhancement' is real-time only on NVIDIA desktop GPUs. Intel's EPE (2021) took about 0.5 s per frame on an RTX 3090, and Intel has discontinued it. REGEN (IEEE Transactions on Games, 2026) distils EPE into a small network that runs at over 20 fps at 960×544 on an RTX 4090 while the same GPU renders UE5. HyPER-GAN (2026) is a lighter U-Net on an RTX 4070 Super. Every published model maps driving footage towards Cityscapes, Mapillary or KITTI; none targets forests. The authors report more flicker when a diffusion model is used as the teacher. The code is public, with ONNX export.

No such enhancer runs at interactive rates on an M2 Air. The best measured real-time diffusion on Apple silicon is 22.7 fps at 512×512 (SDXS-512 through Core ML) on an M3 Ultra with a 60-core GPU; SD-Turbo on MPS took 95.8 ms per frame. The Air has an 8-core GPU of about 2.9 TFLOPS and a 15.8 TOPS Neural Engine. Scaling by GPU size gives about 2–3 fps at 512×512 with Godot not rendering at all; this is my estimate. I found no measured image-translation model reaching 30 fps on an M2.

Cloud real-time video-to-video now exists. Decart's Lucy 2.5 (July 2026) restyles a live WebRTC stream at a claimed 1080p and 30 fps, with about 40 ms of model latency, for $0.02 a second at 720p (about $72 an hour). StreamDiffusionV2 (MLSys 2026) reaches about 42 fps at 480p on one H100 and 16.6 fps on two RTX 4090s. Both see only the colour stream, so they restyle the scene rather than respect its geometry. They also add network latency, and they drift or flicker.

Offline, geometry-conditioned photoreal video is practical now:
- NVIDIA Cosmos-Transfer2.5 (open weights) turns depth, edge, segmentation or blur control videos into photoreal video.
- Cosmos 3 (June 2026, OpenMDW-1.1 licence) includes transfer. Its Edge model makes 121 frames at 480p in about 13 s on an H100, or about 7 s on a B200. That benchmark is image-to-video; transfer mode was not benchmarked.
- NVIDIA warns of temporal inconsistency and object morphing.
This suits stills and fly-throughs rendered from Godot or Cycles passes, not free roam.

Interactive world models look photographic but are not faithful to real places:
- Genie 3 runs at 720p and 20–24 fps and stays consistent for a few minutes. DeepMind says it cannot simulate real-world locations with geographic accuracy.
- Project Genie needs Google AI Ultra ($249.99 a month) and caps worlds at 60 seconds. Its Street View grounding (May 2026) is US-only and cannot be exported.
- Odyssey-2 Pro streams 720p at 22 fps for minutes.
- Tencent HY-World 1.5 has open weights and claims 480p at 24 fps; it needs 28–72 GB of GPU memory, depending on how many GPUs share the model.
None accepts a DEM, a point cloud or a CHM. Waymo's simulator, built on Genie 3, can be grounded in real camera footage, but it is internal to Waymo.

An independent benchmark, WorldRoamBench (June 2026), tested more than 10 world models, Genie 3 included, on 600+ cases with 10–60 s of keyboard control, including nature scenes. None was reliable on action, vision, physics and memory together. Scene-memory scores fell by 37% on average from short to long horizons. A walk across a 5 × 5 km plot would drift.

World Labs comes closest to accepting a real place as input:
- Marble costs $20–95 a month, or about $1.20 a world through the API. It builds a Gaussian-splat world from text, 2–8 photos or a short video. It exports SPZ or PLY splats, a collider mesh and, on Pro, a textured GLB of about 600k triangles. It fills unseen areas generatively.
- Atlas (announced 1 September 2026, early access, no price) takes camera poses and depth maps as inputs, so depth derived from the LiDAR could in principle constrain it. It has no LiDAR input type and reports no metric error.
Under a closed canopy either would invent the trunks and understorey that the airborne LiDAR barely sees, and splats bake in their lighting.

On the M2 (GPU family Apple8), the neural features available save time or memory; none adds realism. From Apple's feature tables:
- MetalFX temporal upscaling needs Apple7 or later. Godot already supports it and the plan uses it.
- MetalFX frame interpolation needs Apple5 or later and a macOS 26 API. Godot does not have it; the only request is a proposal with no maintainer reply.
- MetalFX denoised upscaling needs Apple9 or later, so an M3 or newer.
- Metal 4 tensors and machine-learning encoding need Apple7 or later.
Apple's neural-material demo halves texture memory. The 2026 neural MetalFX upscaler targets the Neural Accelerators on M5 Pro and M5 Max. NVIDIA's neural texture compression, neural materials and radiance cache need Direct3D 12 or Vulkan; the texture-compression SDK lists Windows only.

Godot has no built-in neural inference, but it could host a neural pass:
- CompositorEffect, which is experimental, inserts custom passes into the renderer;
- RenderingDevice.get_driver_resource exposes the native Metal objects, so a GDExtension could hand frames to Core ML or Metal 4.
That would be bespoke C++ and Objective-C work, and no model exists to run at 30 fps on an M2. The community ONNX extensions are experimental.

AI image-to-3D in 2026 helps with rocks, logs and stumps, not trees:
- TRELLIS.2 (Microsoft, MIT licence, 4B parameters) makes PBR-textured meshes in about 60 s on an H100 and needs at least 24 GB of NVIDIA memory. Reviews and later papers report broken branches and poor thin structures.
- The open-weights licence for Hunyuan3D 2.1 excludes the UK, so the owner cannot use it. Versions 3.0 and 3.1 are hosted only.
- Meta's SAM 3D Objects, under a SAM licence that allows commercial use, copes with cluttered photos taken in the field.
- Tree-specific neural methods such as ProcGen3D are still research, tested on synthetic Infinigen trees.
So AI does not remove the tree cap.

AI tools that turn a photo into PBR maps are good enough for moss, lava and litter, with strings attached:
- Ubisoft's CHORD has open weights, but under a research-only copyleft licence.
- Adobe Substance 3D Sampler's Image-to-Material is commercial and runs locally.
The limits are the owner's photos (2000×983, licence unknown) and texel density, not the AI.

Measured this session with tools/lighting_stats.py on the owner's 12 wide photos (U01–U13) and the Godot prototype frames:
- Godot sits inside or at the edge of the photos' range on four metrics: exposure key (photos 0.0060–0.0117, Godot 0.0056–0.0106), sunfleck fraction (0.09–0.22 against 0.08–0.16), black fraction (0.06–0.22 against 0.05–0.27) and highlight B/R (0.69–0.80 against 0.66–0.70).
- Godot falls short on dynamic range (photos 9.6–11.8 stops, Godot 6.5–8.6) and on sky peak (166–244 against 109–132).
- The real photos also fail the gate's warm-highlight target (0.29–0.42), which therefore encodes the UE5.8 look rather than a photographic one. Camera white balance may neutralise warm sun.
By eye, the rest of the gap is structure: many thin, crooked trunks and branches, a mid-storey, moss over lava in fine relief, and litter. The photos' processing is unknown, and JPEG noise inflates their dynamic range.
Renting the GPUs these routes need is cheap per hour. In September 2026 the median on-demand price was $3.25 per GPU-hour for an H100 and $0.67 for an RTX 5090.

The cloud container's egress proxy blocked these hosts: arxiv.org, blog.google, deepmind.google, developer.nvidia.com, research.nvidia.com, worldlabs.ai, fal.ai, techpowerup and cdn-lfs.huggingface.co (where model weights are served). Earlier in the session it also blocked the runpod.io and lambda.ai websites. So this check relied on GitHub, Apple's developer site and search snippets. It also means cloud agents may be unable to fetch model weights or drive rented GPUs unless the owner widens network access.

ratings_or_numbers:
**The M2 Air:** GPU family Apple8, about 2.9 TFLOPS FP32 on the 8-core GPU, and a 15.8 TOPS Neural Engine.

**Real-time enhancement:**
- EPE: about 0.5 s per frame on an RTX 3090.
- REGEN: over 20 fps at 960×544 on an RTX 4090, while also rendering UE5; 32× faster than EPE.
- Real-time diffusion on Apple silicon (M3 Ultra, 60-core GPU): SDXS-512 through Core ML at 22.7 fps at 512×512; SD-Turbo on MPS at 95.8 ms per frame. The M2 Air estimate is about 2–3 fps (judgement).
- DLSS 5: RTX 50 only, shipped 3 September 2026, a reported 40–60% frame-rate cost.
- StreamDiffusionV2 (1.3B model, 480p): 42 fps on one H100, 64.5 fps on four H100s, 16.6 fps on two RTX 4090s.
- AlayaRenderer-Flash: 31.5 fps on one H200. Magpie: about 32 fps on an H100, 34 GB, about 1.55 s input latency.
- Cosmos3-Edge image-to-video, 121 frames at 480p: 7.1 s on a B200, 13.3 s on an H100, 21.9 s on an RTX PRO 6000.
- Decart Lucy 2.5: $0.02 a second at 720p, about $72 an hour.

**World models:**
- Genie 3: 720p at 20–24 fps. Project Genie: 60-second sessions, on Google AI Ultra at $249.99 a month.
- Odyssey-2 Pro: 720p at 22 fps.
- HY-World 1.5: 480p at 24 fps, 28–72 GB of GPU memory.
- WorldRoamBench: scene memory decays 37% on average.
- Marble: $20, $35 or $95 a month; about $1.20 a world through the API.

**Assets and GPU rental:**
- TRELLIS.2: about 60 s per asset at 1536³ on an H100; needs at least 24 GB.
- Median on-demand rent: H100 $3.25 and RTX 5090 $0.67 per GPU-hour.

unknowns: Whether DLSS 5 is available through an SDK to engines other than Unreal and to hobbyists; how good it looks on dense forest (it has only been shown on NBA 2K27 and in demos).
Whether any image-translation network can reach 30 fps on the M2's Neural Engine while Godot renders; no measurement exists.
How well Cosmos transfer does on dense forest at 720p or above, and what a clip costs in transfer mode; only image-to-video was benchmarked.
World Labs Atlas: when it will be generally available, its price, and whether it honours metric depth supplied from outside.
The provenance and licence of the owner's photos, which decide whether they can be used to derive textures or AI assets for this public repository.
Whether Project Genie is available in the UK, and its UK price.

How much work MetalFX frame interpolation would take in Godot's Metal driver, and how it would interact with the frame-pacing issue #114258. It needs macOS 26, and the owner's macOS version is unknown.
Several figures rest on secondary sources or search snippets because the primary pages were blocked by the egress proxy: DLSS 5 cost, Lucy 2.5 pricing, the Genie limits and the Atlas inputs.
verdict_on_photorealism:
No, not for the stated target: free roam on the fanless M2 Air, faithful to the LiDAR. In September 2026 no neural or AI route makes a Godot render read as photographic on that machine.
- **The M2 is too small.** It is one to two orders of magnitude short of the GPUs that run real-time photographic re-rendering (my estimate).
- **Godot has no such path.** Its only neural feature is MetalFX upscaling, which saves time but adds no realism.
- **World models fail the core rule by design.** They invent geometry and drift within minutes.

It is conditionally possible in two other places.
1. **Offline stills and fly-through clips.** Godot or Cycles renders out depth, segmentation and edge passes, and a geometry-conditioned video model (NVIDIA Cosmos Transfer or Cosmos 3) turns them into video on a rented H100 at about $3.25 an hour.
   - The result looks photographic.
   - Terrain and trunk layout hold at the scale of the control maps, but bark, moss and small plants are invented.
   - Expect flicker and morphing, at 480–720p.
2. **Interactive, in either of two ways:**
   - **an RTX 50 Windows PC with DLSS 5-class neural rendering.** It is shipping today but not available to Godot; it would need a Streamline integration in a Godot fork, with SDK access unverified;
   - **the Godot window streamed through a cloud video-to-video model.** Lucy 2.5 costs about $72 an hour at 720p; expect added latency, drift and geometry that no longer matches the LiDAR.

On the Air, AI can raise realism only through content (rocks, logs, stumps, PBR materials), and the trees still cap it.

Measured this session: Godot's global lighting statistics already overlap the owner's photos. The remaining gap is structure and dynamic range, which content and exposure work must close, not a neural filter.
what_it_would_take: **On the M2, keep the neural part to MetalFX Temporal**, as planned. Optionally add MetalFX frame interpolation through a patch to Godot's Metal driver: an estimated 1–2 agent sessions. It needs macOS 26 and risks frame pacing. It buys frame rate, not realism.

**For interactive photographic output, choose one of two routes:**
- **(a) An RTX 50 PC and DLSS 5.** This needs UE5, which the owner has excluded, or a Streamline and Direct3D 12 integration in a Godot fork with unverified SDK access. High cost and high risk.
- **(b) Stream the Godot window through a cloud video-to-video model.** Lucy 2.5 costs about $1.20 a minute at 720p. Expect latency, drift and loss of geometric fidelity.

Neither route works on the M2 Air.

**Treat world models as mood boards, not the product.** Revisit World Labs Atlas once it is priced, to test small splat vignettes at trail spots conditioned on LiDAR depth. Label them as synthetic and keep them out of the measured world.
